definition: Plummet means to fall steeply and very fast.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word plummet. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know plummet should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: When the crane's cable slipped, the piano plummeted six stories and burst on the pavement like a dropped crate of bells.
A slip is far milder than a plummet — a small loss of footing or a few points shed, quickly caught.
A tumble is milder than a plummet — a real fall, but a bumping, partial one, while a plummet drops sheer and unchecked to the bottom.

A plunge is just as steep and fast as a plummet, but it can be chosen: a hand plunged into icy water, a country plunged into reform by its own vote. Plummet keeps no such option — what plummets is falling helplessly, like a stone let go.

A nosedive borrows the aircraft's picture — a nose tipping down into a sudden steep drop — and it is the favorite word for numbers: sales, ratings, stocks. Plummet describes the same steepness for anything at all, and its falls read as sheer and unbroken rather than tipped.

A crash is a fall named by its ending — the impact, the wreck, the ruin at the bottom. Plummet is the fall itself, the sheer unbraked descent, and says nothing about how it ends; a market can plummet for a week before anyone calls it a crash.
